milestones.label: Earliest claim for Social Security retirement benefits
milestones.population: workers who are fully insured under Social Security
whatChanges: A fully insured worker may first file for retirement benefits, and the monthly amount is permanently reduced relative to filing at full retirement age.
Filing here is one option among several; many people file later, and never filing at this point is an ordinary path.

milestones.label: Full retirement age for Social Security
milestones.population: people who reach early retirement age after the statutory transition date set in federal law
whatChanges: Retirement benefits become payable without the reduction that federal law applies to earlier filing.
Statute raised this age in steps across successive birth cohorts, and the figure here is the top of that schedule.
It also sets the starting point for the credits that federal law grants for postponing a claim.

milestones.label: Delayed retirement credits stop accruing
milestones.population: people who are fully insured and eligible for old-age benefits but do not receive them
whatChanges: The credits that raise a monthly benefit for each month of postponement stop being earned, so postponing further adds nothing under this rule.
People who claimed earlier and then suspended their benefits to earn these credits also stop accruing them here.
Earning any of these credits at all is optional, and many people never do.

milestones.label: Medicare eligibility
milestones.population: people who meet the citizenship or residency requirements set in federal law
whatChanges: Federal health insurance becomes available to people who meet the citizenship or residency requirements.
Enrollment runs on its own federal timetable, separate from when a person claims Social Security retirement benefits.
Separate federal routes into the program exist that do not depend on age at all.

milestones.label: Age route to Social Security widow's or widower's benefits
milestones.careNote: This is a benefits rule, not guidance for grief and not a statement of what anyone owes a spouse who died; the pages on a death and on grief are the route for that.
milestones.population: widows and widowers of workers who died fully insured, on the age route the regulation states
whatChanges: A widow or widower may file for survivors benefits on this route, subject to the marriage-duration and remarriage conditions the regulation sets out.
The same regulation states a separate, earlier route for a widow or widower who has a disability as it defines one.
Federal rules also govern how this benefit interacts with a person's own retirement benefit.
